statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-118380: libgssrpc used the unverified RPCSEC_GSS service type sent during context establishment, instead of the verified one in each request, to decide how to unwrap call arguments and wrap results, so an active network attacker could alter the arguments a legitimate client sends to an RPCSEC_GSS-protected service or cause results to be sent unprotected. MIT fixed it in krb5 1.22.3, whose announcement lists this CVE: https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html. The fix is commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/d6849c7c5fb388ba7f48d4d773bb940ecdbc993e on the krb5-1.22 branch, contained in the krb5-1.22.3-final tag and not in krb5-1.22.2-final; in src/lib/rpc/svc_auth_gss.c it adds svcauth_gss_check_call(), which gssrpc__svcauth_gss() now uses to verify each call and take the service level from the verified credential, and its other changes are tests. Alpine's krb5 1.22.3-r0 on the 3.23-stable branch upgrades to MIT 1.22.3 and lists CVE-2026-118380 under 1.22.3-r0 in its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/2cb5928755d78bc5381941f16adedf76bfbcde96/main/krb5/APKBUILD. The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository (main and security, x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source krb5 at 1.22.1-r0 and 1.22.3-r0 (plus krb5-conf 1.0-r2, which holds only configuration). The libkrb5 library in the krb5-libs package reports krb5-1.22.3-final in the 1.22.3-r0 build and krb5-1.22.1-final in 1.22.1-r0, on both architectures, each package verified against its index checksum. 1.22.1-r0 is MIT 1.22.1, which predates the fix, so it is affected; the range ends at 1.22.3-r0, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-118380: libgssrpc used the unverified RPCSEC_GSS service type sent during context establishment, instead of the verified one in each request, to decide how to unwrap call arguments and wrap results, so an active network attacker could alter the arguments a legitimate client sends to an RPCSEC_GSS-protected service or cause results to be sent unprotected. MIT fixed it in krb5 1.22.3, whose announcement lists this CVE: https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html. The fix is commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/d6849c7c5fb388ba7f48d4d773bb940ecdbc993e on the krb5-1.22 branch, contained in the krb5-1.22.3-final tag and not in krb5-1.22.2-final; in src/lib/rpc/svc_auth_gss.c it adds svcauth_gss_check_call(), which gssrpc__svcauth_gss() now uses to verify each call and take the service level from the verified credential, and its other changes are tests. Debian fixed it for trixie in 1.21.3-5+deb13u2 (DSA-6650-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-118380. The DHI Debian repository publishes three rebuilds of Debian's 1.21.3-5+deb13u1 and one rebuild of Debian's fixed 1.21.3-5+deb13u2. We checked every binary package of these four builds, including libgssrpc4t64, libkrb5-3 and the libkrb5-dbg debug symbols, for amd64 and arm64, each verified against its index checksum, with function sizes read from the debug symbols: of the three rebuilds of 1.21.3-5+deb13u1, only the third's libgssrpc.so.4.2 contains svcauth_gss_check_call() (719 bytes on amd64, 624 on arm64), the first two lack it, and the third rebuild's package changelog records the backport of this fix. In the rebuild of 1.21.3-5+deb13u2 libgssrpc.so.4.2 contains svcauth_gss_check_call() with the same size (719 and 624 bytes), and its changelog lists this CVE. The range ends at the third rebuild of 1.21.3-5+deb13u1, the first published build with the fix; the later rebuild of 1.21.3-5+deb13u2 also carries it.
